title: Workflow to make sprites with codex into ComfyUI locally?
author: SpaghettiMan247
selftext:
I’m trying to build a local sprite pipeline with ComfyUI and Codex. I’ve got Codex connected to Comfy and can move files back and forth, run workflows, etc. Hardware is an RTX 4080 16GB.  
The goal is pretty specific: take an existing painted RPG character sprite, keep the same character/style, generate controlled animation poses, and ideally later swap armor/weapons/helmets without redrawing everything.  
So far I’ve tried SDXL + img2img + OpenPose/ControlNet and I’m not getting anything I’d actually ship. Identity/style drifts too much once I force a new pose.  
Before I spend more time inventing a workflow, is anyone already doing something close to this locally? Especially interested in documented Comfy workflows for:

character consistency across animation frames  
pose control  
equipment/outfit changes  
transparent sprite output / sprite sheets

I’m not looking for a cloud solution right now. Mostly trying to find out whether there’s an existing local workflow I should be building on instead of reinventing this.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
The short answer is that you have the right idea, but this won't work because the technology (diffusion models) are fighting the intent (consistency).

I'm doing something similar as a proof of concept, and the step that makes it work at all is img2video.  

Generate reference images with SDXL + my style lora, feed those into an R2V workflow that generates a single 15 second video of the full looping animation at various angles, chop that up into individual frames and clean it/build sprite sheets out of it.

It's finicky, and if you ever expect something consistent and production quality it'll need loras trained for your style and every single character, but it's the only way to keep consistent character details through multiple angles of the same action animation.

replies.author: SpaghettiMan247
replies.body: I like this, worth exploring at least, thanks!
